q-70072.name: Question 1
q-70072.worked_solution:
Writing $z$ as $\frac{z}{1}$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{9}z & =\frac{4}{9}\cdot z \\  & =\frac{4}{9}\cdot \frac{z}{1} \\  & =\frac{4\cdot z}{9\cdot 1} \\  & =\frac{4z}{9}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the expressions $\frac{4}{9}z$ and $\frac{4z}{9}$ are equivalent.

q-108696.name: Question 3
q-108696.worked_solution:
First, remember that the product of a positive number and a negative number is a negative number. Thus, 

$$
\frac{1}{7}(-f)=-\frac{1}{7}f.
$$

Now, writing $f$ as $\frac{f}{1},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{7}f & =-\frac{1}{7}\cdot f \\  & =-\frac{1}{7}\cdot \frac{f}{1} \\  & =-\frac{1\cdot f}{7\cdot 1} \\  & =-\frac{f}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the expressions $\frac{1}{7}(-f)$ and $-\frac{f}{7}$ are equivalent.

q-100026.name: Question 4
q-100026.worked_solution:
First, remember that the product of two negative numbers is a positive number. Thus, 

$$
-\frac{7}{4}(-h)=\frac{7}{4}h.
$$

Now, writing $h$ as $\frac{h}{1},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{7}{4}h & =\frac{7}{4}\cdot h \\  & =\frac{7}{4}\cdot \frac{h}{1} \\  & =\frac{7\cdot h}{4\cdot 1} \\  & =\frac{7h}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
